questions.text: The formula y ~ x1 * x2 expands to which model equation?
options: y = β₀ + β₁x₁ + β₂x₂ + β₃x₁x₂ + ε
questions.explanation: In R, x1 * x2 is shorthand for x1 + x2 + x1:x2. The ':' operator creates the product term x1×x2. So y ~ x1 * x2 fits the model with both main effects (x1 and x2) and their interaction (x1×x2), with four total parameters: β₀, β₁, β₂, β₃.

questions.text: In the formula y ~ x^2, R creates a column containing x².
questions.explanation: In R formulas, the '^' operator means 'crossing up to degree k', not arithmetic exponentiation. y ~ x^2 is treated the same as y ~ x. To create a literal x² column, write y ~ I(x^2). The I() function protects the arithmetic from the formula parser.

questions.text: In lm(log(price) ~ log(carat) * cut), the coefficient for 'log(carat):cutIdeal' is −0.08. How do you interpret this?
options: Ideal diamonds cost 8% less than Fair diamonds per carat
The slope of log(carat) is 0.08 log-units lower for Ideal-cut diamonds than for Fair-cut diamonds — Ideal diamonds have a slightly smaller price elasticity for carat
Ideal diamonds have a price that is 0.08 log-units higher than Fair after controlling for carat
The interaction term means the model predicts negative prices for some Ideal diamonds
questions.explanation: The interaction coefficient log(carat):cutIdeal = −0.08 means the slope of log(carat) decreases by 0.08 for Ideal vs Fair diamonds. The effective slope for Ideal is β₁ + (−0.08). This captures the idea that Ideal diamonds derive less incremental value from additional carat weight — their quality premium is partly independent of size.

questions.text: In a prediction grid plot with colour = cut and facet by model (additive vs interaction), what visual pattern confirms that the interaction matters?
options: All lines in both panels are horizontal
Lines are parallel in both panels
Lines are parallel in the additive panel but fan out (non-parallel) in the interaction panel
The interaction panel has fewer lines
questions.explanation: The additive model forces parallel lines by construction (one shared slope). The interaction model allows each group to have its own slope. If the interaction is meaningful, the lines in the interaction panel will be non-parallel — they diverge or converge across the range of x.

questions.text: You fit poly(log(carat), 2, raw = TRUE) and get coefficients β₁ = 1.80 for log(carat) and β₂ = −0.10 for log(carat)². What does β₂ < 0 mean?
options: The price-carat relationship is increasing at a decreasing rate on the log scale — concave
The model predicts negative prices for large diamonds
The quadratic term is not significant
questions.explanation: A negative quadratic coefficient β₂ < 0 means the parabola opens downward — the log-price increases with log(carat) but the rate of increase slows down (concave). Equivalently, each additional percentage increase in carat yields progressively smaller percentage gains in price beyond the main linear effect.

questions.text: An interaction model y ~ x1 * x2 always has lower AIC than the additive model y ~ x1 + x2, because it has more parameters.
questions.explanation: Lower AIC means better model, and AIC penalises extra parameters with +2k. Adding an interaction term improves fit (reduces RSS) but also increases k. If the improvement in −2log(L̂) is less than 2 (the penalty per parameter), AIC will be higher for the interaction model — the simpler additive model is preferred.
